title: Introduction to Tables
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of introduction to tables in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: A data table is a grid of relationships. Correct header cells and captions make those relationships available beyond visual styling.
content.why_it_matters: Tables and forms carry structured data. Semantic relationships and understandable constraints improve both usability and the reliability of information sent to an application.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: When tables are appropriate is one of the decisions covered by Introduction to Tables. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: The <table> element
items.text: A table presents data with meaningful row-column relationships, not general visual page layout.

items.title: The <td> element
items.text: A table data cell holds a value in the table grid.

items.title: The <th> element
items.text: A table header cell provides labels for the cells associated with it.

items.title: Tables versus lists and layout containers
items.text: Use list markup when items form a genuine group. Choose ordered lists when sequence matters, unordered lists when it does not, and description lists for terms with associated descriptions.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Introduction to Tables is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.
Use list markup when items form a genuine group. Choose ordered lists when sequence matters, unordered lists when it does not, and description lists for terms with associated descriptions.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
